text: The impression of authenticity about a person. <break time="0.8s" /> Results from an evaluation by the perceiver. <break time="0.8s" /> That the information derived from that person. <break time="0.8s" /> Can be used to take adaptive decisions. <break time="0.8s" /> Such information is available. <break time="0.8s" /> Through two categories of indicators. <break time="0.8s" /> Cues and signals. <break time="0.8s" /> Cues are features of the environment. <break time="0.8s" /> That have not necessarily evolved for communication purposes. <break time="0.8s" /> But that nonetheless convey information. <break time="0.8s" /> In other words. <break time="0.8s" /> A social cue is an opportunity. <break time="0.8s" /> For receivers to extract information about an individual. <break time="0.8s" /> Possibly with the aid of contextual indicators. <break time="0.8s" /> And some basic rules about the relationships between these indicators. <break time="0.8s" /> The second source of information about individuals. <break time="0.8s" /> Is social signals. <break time="0.8s" /> Social signals are actions or structures. <break time="0.8s" /> That evolved as a result of their effect on other organisms. <break time="0.8s" /> Even though signals might not always contain information. <break time="0.8s" /> Or act in the benefit of the receiver. <break time="0.8s" /> Signaling is expected to be reliable. <break time="0.8s" /> Whenever the costs of deceptive signals. <break time="0.8s" /> Exceed the benefits of providing honest cues.
